correctness.rationale: For Omega<=4 the prime-factorization shape partition is complete. Multiplicative prime-power formulas establish the sign of all squarefree, prime-power, and p^2q^2 shapes, and solve p^a q for a=2,3. For p^2 q r the product identity forces q,r>(p^2+1)/(p-1), excludes p=2, and for odd p forces B=(p^2+1)/2 to divide the squarefree qr with 1<B<qr, hence B=q or r. Cancellation yields (p-3)r=p^2+3; then p=3 is impossible and p-3|12 gives only p=5,7, both contradicted by primality. Finite independent direct arithmetic checked 737449 tested n with Omega<=4 through 10^6; no finite check is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Trudgian explicitly asks about existence and infinitude of equal divisor sums. Omega is a canonical prime-factor multiplicity measure; locating the entire first four layers is a complete and natural small-complexity classification, not a numerical table. The p^2qr forced-prime obstruction eliminates an infinite three-prime-support family not covered by known singleton-cofactor results, and sharp cases 20 and45 explain the threshold. No paper-sized contribution or global infinitude resolution is claimed.
